items.title: Binding nick; agent name and nick editable
items.box:
Binding nick; agent name and nick editable.

WHAT THE DESK DOES (decided by Andy, 2026-10-13)

The agent's pane in Desk
- Row one: name and nick (text inputs). Row two: the toggles included and cap; more toggles may follow. Written by Andy alone; every agent may read every pane.
- The nick is Andy's shorthand for addressing a key in a few keystrokes. The desk knows it; the agent need not.

Names and keys
- The page shows the agent's name everywhere it shows the agent: chat lines, presence bubble, Team list, taker marks. The name is looked up by the agent's key; the node's label is shown only when no name is set. Keys are never shown on the page.
- Under the hood every chat line carries its writer's key, and every decision about who goes by key: take, nick address, block, the one box write.

The binding nick
- A line of Andy's starting with a nick followed by any punctuation or a space is addressed to that agent alone: only it is notified, only it may take it.
- A nick request about the box hands the box to that agent for one write: the box turns red at once, awaiting that agent; nobody else takes it meanwhile, Andy included; the hold ends when the write lands or after one minute. A write the desk refuses does not use up the one update.

included
- Off: the agent still reads everything, every write of it is refused, and its bubble shows absent. It is the desk's own signoff and overrules the agent's own connect (deskUnsloth cannot bring an excluded agent back).

cap
- On: a "cap" from Andy with no nick offers the box to every agent with cap on; the first to take it holds it under the one-write rule above.
- Off: that agent gets a cap only when addressed by its nick.

Not in this item
- A rules text per agent was dropped: the desk can only gate what it accepts, not make an agent read. Levant is steered by the context deskUnsloth sends him on every call.

FOUND (Andy's desk, 2026-10-13; paths under spirit/run/)
- The pane already has name, nick and save (shell/desk/desk.js, deskAgentProfileSave), stored by the owner-only profile.set (process/js/desk/desk.js), keyed by the agent's key; a nick is 1 to 8 of a-z and 0-9.
- The name is shown nowhere today: lines, bubbles and takers show the node's label for the key (writerOf); for Levant, "ollama agent node".
- The nick takes a line only after a colon, and every connected agent still receives it.
- The desk's records store each chat line's label and key; the item built from them keeps only label, time and text.

items.title: Red Q checks only on purpose
items.box:
Red Q checks only on purpose.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
- A red Q is a concise question placed with deliberation, to block an item until it is resolved.
- A question mark in a chat line never makes a red Q; only a deliberate Q check does.
- One open red Q per agent per item: a second is refused until the first is answered or cleared.
- A Q longer than one sentence, or over about 200 bytes, is refused with a why.
- Andy clears them himself: Q:clear deletes every red Q on the item; Q<n>:clear deletes only that one.
- When Andy clears a Q, the agent that placed it is notified; a clear is a form of reply, so the agent updates its position on that question.
- A red Q clicked into Andy's chat box arrives followed by two newlines, so the question stands apart from the answer he writes below it.

FOUND (2026-10-13)
- Today the desk turns any chat line ending in a question mark into a red Q check, and each open red Q holds up Go and other presses.

items.title: Verifier fixes
items.box:
Verifier fixes.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
- The Verifier tab stays once the page has loaded; only the first ask at load decides whether a verifier runs here. A later missed answer keeps the tab and shows "not answering".
- Every press in the tab shows at once that it was sent, then what deskVerify answered.
- A Stop is kept for the whole run, whenever it is pressed (a suite running, pulling, between suites, waiting for a commit), and deskVerify checks it before each suite; the tab shows "stop asked" until the run ends.
- deskVerify answers at once even mid-run: the git work that blocks it now (pull, ancestry checks) no longer freezes it.
- deskVerify keeps, beside each failing test's outcome, its failure text (capped), so the why is in the record and nobody has to rerun a suite to read it.
- deskVerify answers one search verb, bucket-bounded with the partial flag, over two things: tests and suites (the official latest state of a single test, or of every test in a suite: outcome, commit, time, failure text; filtered by suite, test words, outcome, commit, item, since), and runs (each check it made, item or full run: commit, queued, started, ended, its outcome and the line it posted; filtered by item, commit, kind, since). The same verb runs on every node's deskVerify, so an agent asks Andy's (the official record) and its own; agents may call it, nothing is written through it.
- The idle hour comes back and its chores are done (goal/G8.4, never built until now): a node is idle after an hour with no desk write and no phase held by its agent; then its deskVerify runs publishData for its agent (measure, write agents/<agent-name>/, commit under the standing grant) and writes the test-state report from its own dataset, never by re-running suites. All code, no model. The tab's countdown counts to that hour and shows what the chores did.

FOUND (Andy's node, 2026-10-13; paths under spirit/run/)
- shell/desk/desk.js, deskAskVerifier: any failed "now" ask sets the verifier to none and redraws the tabs, so the tab disappears; every press and every opening of the tab asks again.
- The Stop and Full run presses send and show nothing until the next answer.
- process/js/deskVerify/deskVerify.js, stopRun: Stop is accepted only while a suite process runs; at any other moment it answers not stopped and is forgotten.
- deskVerify pulls and checks ancestry with spawnSync, which blocks it while git works.
- Measured idle: four now-asks answered in 11 to 56 ms.

chat.text: Does the verifier have a query/db set of verbs?

- Its db holds two tables: results (each test outcome as it flips) and runs (every check, queued, waiting, running, ended, with its commit).
- Its verbs today are only now, stop, full.run and record. No query verb: records.search went in G19.11 because only tests called it.
- So nothing outside it can search its results or its runs right now; a bucket-bounded search verb over both would be the place for that, if you want it in this item.
so how do agents know which suites/tests fail? what the official records (the desk verifiers) say at any moment?

Today they mostly cannot:
- The only official word is the line deskVerify posts on an item when it checks it (passed, or rejected with the red suite and its first failures) and the item status.
- There is no way to ask what is red right now across the tree; agents run suites in their own clones, which is not your record.
- Proposed for this item: one read verb on deskVerify, a bucket-bounded search over its results giving each matching suite and test with its latest outcome, commit and time, with the partial flag; agents may call it, nobody writes through it.
so the agent has go figure out what went wrong by manually running suites?

Yes, today they do. The verifier keeps per test only its title, outcome, commit and time; the failure text it prints is thrown away after the first lines go into the item chat. So to see why, an agent reruns the suite in its own clone, on its own tree, which may not be yours.
- The read verb fixes the which; for the why, the verifier would also have to keep each failing test failure text (capped) beside its outcome, so the agent reads your record instead of rerunning.

put a damn search with filters etc so you can get that info quick, from the offical (desk) verifier and from your own.

Makes sense. Recorded (box v2): failure text kept beside each failing test, and a search with filters (suite, test words, outcome, commit, item, since) on every node deskVerify, yours the official one.
run-details, official state of single tests or suites?

- runs: each check the verifier made (item or full run, commit, queued, started, ended, the outcome and the line it posted), filtered by item, commit, kind and since.
Say yes and both go in the box as one search verb that answers either.

items.title: Chat flow; one task per agent
items.box:
Chat flow; one task per agent.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
The chat flow
- Each of Andy's lines is taken by one agent and answered by that agent alone; no other agent chimes in once it is taken.
- An agent's answer is never takeable: no agent answers another agent. A second answer comes only when Andy asks for it by naming the agent.
- Why: an answer must not scroll away while he reads it.
- An agent may post its own work notes (taking, built, claimed) on an item it holds; they are valued work logs and are not answers, so the chat flow does not stop them.
One task at a time
- An agent holds one task, one item and one phase, at a time; taking a second is refused by the desk until the first is released, claimed or done. Seen: an agent holding two reds blocked another agent from working.
- Excluding an agent releases what it holds: its task and phase are free for another agent to take.

FOUND (2026-10-13)
- Only Andy's latest line is taken (goal/G18.8); an agent holding the item may still post freely, and agent lines are not taken at all.
- Every desk record keeps the writer's key beside the label shown.
